_comment: Reference data for tools/evidence_import.py (`intel.py evidence import <case> <findings.json>` / the evidence_import @tool). An analyst's graded findings are stored under cases/<case>/evidence/imported/ and written into the KB with the provenance tag below so assessments can cite them. Rung semantics come from rungs.json (owner = edge; kit / neighbour = fact only, RULE 5) — this file only holds the grading vocabulary and provenance labels. RULE 1: grading vocabulary only, never case data.

admiralty._comment: Admiralty (NATO) grade accepted on an imported finding: source reliability A-F + information credibility 1-6, e.g. B2. `pattern` is matched against the grade after upper-casing and stripping spaces / hyphens. A finding with no grade, or one that does not match, is REJECTED with a message — an ungraded claim cannot be cited.

reliability_confidence._comment: Source-reliability letter -> KB confidence word (knowledge_base.CONF_WORDS) for the facts and edges an imported finding writes. A/B are reliable sources, C fairly reliable, D-F not usually reliable / unreliable / cannot be judged.

provenance._comment: KB provenance labels: `source` is the tag every fact/edge carries (the harness assessment cites imported evidence by it); `collector` names this importer; `fact_attribute` is the attribute an indicator's finding is stored under; `default_rel` labels an owner selector_link that gave no rel.

attribute_rows._comment: Optional `attributes` rows on a finding ({entity, attribute, value, valid_from?, valid_until?}) set a KB attribute at the ANALYST authority tier (kb_memory.json), whatever the Admiralty grade (the grade only sets confidence). A single-valued attribute is reconciled — it supersedes, corrects or is disputed against the standing value; any other attribute is added as a plain analyst fact. `name_pattern` is the accepted attribute-name shape; `reserved` names belong to the importer and RULE 5 (link facts, rung labels) and are refused, so a row can never forge a kit/neighbour link or an analyst_finding.

finding_fields._comment: Optional per-finding report fields. `confirmation` is the analyst's confirmation level for the claim (an unknown value is dropped with a note; the finding still imports); `not_proven` is the boundary sentence — what the evidence does NOT show — rendered under the finding in the house report. Neither is ever written to the KB.

report_sections._comment: Schema of the optional top-level `report` block ({"findings": [...], "report": {...}}). Each key is a list of rows; a malformed row is REJECTED with a message and the rest import; an unknown key is rejected whole. `required` keys must be non-empty; `enums` are matched case-insensitively (priority upper-cased); `patterns` are regexes on the stripped value (case-sensitive); `dates` must be ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD or a full date-time); `lists` accept a list of strings or one string; `numbers` must be JSON numbers; `raw_lists` are lists of strings/numbers stored as-is; `objects` are lists of sub-rows validated with their own spec; a duplicate `id` inside one import is rejected. Rows are stored inside the same content-addressed imported record and read back by tools/report_sections.py. RULE 5: report rows NEVER touch the KB — not even `roles`, which are analyst judgement for the report only, nor `metrics.values`, which may hold secrets and are kept only for the anti-inflation duplicate check (never printed in the report).

subject_profile._comment: Identity card rows. `entity` defaults to "subject". basis + source are REQUIRED on alias and relative rows (an unsourced alias / relative is how a wrong person enters a profile); other fields are linted, not rejected, when unsourced. Analyst judgement for the report only — never the KB (RULE 5).

client_seeds._comment: Details the CLIENT supplied at intake. Rendered in Methodology; sensitive=true values are withheld unless house_report --show-sensitive. Never the KB.

engagement._comment: ONE object (kind=object), not a list: document-control metadata for the report front matter. The latest import wins.
